data.title: Flip-Flop Plinko
data.statement:
A vertical board of W columns and H rows is studded with pegs. Each cell is either empty (.)
or holds a peg: < deflects a ball to the left, > deflects it to the right.

You drop N balls one at a time into column C, from above the top row. On each row, from top
to bottom:
- if the cell at the ball's column is empty, the ball falls straight down to the next row;
- otherwise the ball falls diagonally to the next row, one column to the left for < or one
column to the right for >, and the peg it just hit immediately flips to point the other way.

The board is never reset: every ball falls through the pegs exactly as the previous balls
have flipped them.

Print the column each ball comes out of.
data.constraints:
3 <= W <= 30
1 <= H <= 20
1 <= N <= 50
0 <= C < W
No peg stands in column 0 or column W-1, so a ball can never leave the board sideways.

STATEMENT
Drop the balls one by one and print the column each of them comes out of.
INPUT
w: board width
h: board height
n: number of balls
c: the column the balls are dropped into
row: one row of the board, made of ., < and > characters
OUTPUT
n lines: for each ball, the column it comes out of
data.inputDescription:
Line 1: four space-separated integers W (width), H (height), N (number of balls) and C (the
column the balls are dropped into).
Next H lines: one row of the board, W characters, each of them ., < or >. The first of these
lines is the top row.
data.outputDescription:
N lines: for each ball, in the order they are dropped, the column it comes out of. Columns
are numbered from 0.
